q: When we arrived at the station, the train ___.
e: The train left before we arrived: past perfect.

q: While I ___ dinner, the phone rang.
e: Action in progress interrupted by another: past continuous.

q: She was exhausted because she ___ all night.
e: A long activity before a past moment: past perfect continuous.

q: He opened the door, ___ his coat and sat down.
e: Events in sequence: past simple.

q: By 1990, the population ___ to five million.
e: 'By' + a past date: past perfect.

q: I ___ snow before I moved to Canada.
e: Experience up to a past moment: past perfect.

q: This time last year, I ___ for my final exams.
e: In progress at a specific past moment: past continuous.

q: I didn't recognise him because he ___ (grow) a beard.
e: The beard grew before I saw him: past perfect.

q: The streets were wet because it ___ (rain) all morning.
e: Earlier activity that explains a past situation.

q: While they ___ (walk) home, it started to snow.
e: Background action: past continuous.

q: When I got to the cinema, I realised I ___ (leave) my ticket at home.
e: Leaving the ticket happened first: past perfect.

q: In 2005 the city ___ (build) its first metro line.
e: A single finished event with a date: past simple.

q: When I was a child, I ___ (go) to my grandmother's house every Sunday.
e: Past habit: past simple, 'used to' or 'would'. Not past continuous.

q: When I arrived, they already ate all the food.
fix: When I arrived, they had already eaten all the food.
e: Eating finished before I arrived: past perfect.

q: I was knowing the answer, but I stayed silent.
fix: I knew the answer, but I stayed silent.
e: 'Know' is a state verb: no continuous form.

q: She told me that she has lost her passport the day before.
fix: She told me that she had lost her passport the day before.
e: Reported speech about an earlier event: past perfect.

q: Before I came to London, I never used the underground.
fix: Before I came to London, I had never used the underground.
e: Experience up to a past moment: had never + participle.

q: First the film started. Then we arrived.
hint: Use the past perfect. Begin: When we arrived, the film ...
a: When we arrived, the film had started.
When we arrived, the film had already started.
e: The earlier action takes the past perfect.

q: He studied for six hours. Then he fell asleep.
hint: Begin: He fell asleep after he ...
a: He fell asleep after he had studied for six hours.
He fell asleep after he had been studying for six hours.
He fell asleep after he studied for six hours.
e: After + past perfect shows the earlier action.

q: I was reading. In the middle of this, the lights went out.
a: I was reading when the lights went out.
e: Past continuous (background) + when + past simple (event).
